Choosing TRD-018 in the dropdown left that 5 in place. Selling 4 units then invoiced 20.00 against a cost of 1,347.44. The ledger was right; the screen let a real mistake through silently. The same pattern existed in Purchase Entry, where the unit cost did not follow the item either. Changes: * The price follows the item in Sales Entry, defaulting to that item's average cost so the user starts from break-even and raises it. * The unit cost follows the item in Purchase Entry, for the same reason. * An added line seeds its price from the item rather than zero. * A below-cost sale is now reported. It is not blocked, because a clearance sale is legitimate, but the preview carries a warning naming the item, the price, the cost, and the size of the loss. A zero price reads as "no sale price" rather than as an enormous percentage. * Sales Entry displayed no warnings at all; it does now, and a negative gross profit is shown in red. Tests: * frontend/src/features/sales/SalesPage.test.tsx renders the screen and drives the dropdown. It fails against the previous code with exactly the reported symptom: expected '5.00000000' to be '336.86047000'. * backend/tests/test_sales_posting.py covers the below-cost flag, a sale at cost, and the zero-price wording. Shell(cd /Users/rezuan/Rezuan/projects/commandcode-test-project && git commit -F - <<'EOF' Support Postgres so posted data survives a restart Reported from the deployed demo: after posting a purchase, a production run and a sale, the Inventory screen showed TRD-018 back to 0. The data was gone. The ledger was correct. On Render's free plan there is no persistent disk, so the SQLite file lives on the container filesystem. The instance sleeps after about 15 minutes idle, and on wake the container is rebuilt from the image and the database re-seeds from the workbook. The work was never lost to a bug; it was lost to the hosting plan. That is fine for a guided session and wrong for a link left with the client, who will read a silent reset as a broken system. Running the books on a hosted Postgres fixes it without changing the API. * Adds psycopg to backend/requirements.txt. * config.py rewrites postgres:// and postgresql:// to the installed driver, so a connection string from a host like Neon can be pasted unchanged. * clear_all_data() in core/db.py deletes rows, children before parents, using the metadata's dependency sort. That last one fixes a real defect found while testing. The demo reset used DROP TABLE, which needs an exclusive lock, so on Postgres it blocked behind any session holding a read lock — which a serving application always has. Pressing "Reset demo data" against Postgres would have hung the demo indefinitely. Row deletion takes only a row lock, is compatible with readers, and completes in under a second. The test suite hangs on Postgres without this change. conftest.py accepts RPCI_TEST_DATABASE_URL so the whole suite runs against either engine. Verified: 59 tests pass on SQLite and on Postgres; the app boots on Postgres and reproduces every workbook figure; the worked example runs there unchanged; and a posted purchase survives killing and restarting the server, which is the behaviour this change exists to provide. DEPLOYMENT.md option C is rewritten with the Neon steps, .env.example and render.yaml document the choice, and the README covers both engines. Co-authored-by: CommandCodeBot <noreply@commandcode.ai> EOF echo "--- committed ---" && git log --oneline -4)
